A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgentBreeder framework and experiments. The text, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching reordered experiments and v1 Appendices A–C to their counterparts in v2.

before.justification: V1 Sections 5.1–5.3 and Tables 1–3 report original benchmark evaluations of scaffolds discovered by Capable, Blue, and Red AgentBreeder.

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark evaluations and adds evolutionary-population results in Appendix A, Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the three optimization modes, mutation and crossover instructions, embedding descriptors, clustering, and Pareto selection are retained. The added self-improvement terminology and red-mode prompt explanation do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DROP, MMLU, GPQA, attack-enhanced SaladData, and TruthfulQA, with red-mode optimization using DROP and inverted SaladData. The new evolution plots cover these existing experiments; the benchmark descriptions move from Appendix A to B.

E2.justification: The blue and red comparisons retain the same seven seed scaffolds, and the capability-only experiment retains its seed and ADAS comparators. PromptBreeder is newly discussed in related work but is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported generation budgets, validation sampling, models, and evaluation metrics are retained. Blue and red tables still use 250 held-out test samples, while the capability-only table uses 500. The new figures show the existing 20-generation blue and 10-generation red searches.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix A adds generation-colored population plots and seed-versus-evolved Pareto frontiers for the blue and red searches, documenting search behavior beyond final scores. The capability-only experiment renamed 'Multi-Objective Ablation' was already present and interpreted as an ablation in v1.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix E explicitly reports one search run per benchmark and mode, while v1's unspecified claim of consistency across repeated runs is removed. Bootstrap confidence-interval reporting remains unchanged. This changes run disclosure without establishing an increase or decrease in replication.

E6.justification: All corresponding benchmark scores and confidence intervals are unchanged after matching v1 Tables 1, 2, 3 to v2 Tables 3, 1, 2. V2 adds population-level results in Figures 2–3 and derived percentage comparisons, including 79.4% average safety uplift and 21.0% GPQA uplift; these are newly reported summaries, not improved scores between versions.

T1.justification: The Pareto-optimality definitions and algorithmic mathematics are retained, with no added theorem, assumption, proof, or derivation. Mathematical row labels in v2's tables replace descriptive scaffold-selection labels rather than introducing new formal results.

C1.justification: The attack, defense, and evaluation contributions remain. V2 strengthens the headline account by claiming 79.4% average safety uplift alongside maintained or improved capability, with maximum safety and GPQA percentage gains added to the conclusion. V1 emphasized competitive performance and marginal capability improvements more cautiously.

C2.justification: V2 Section 5.2 adds the interpretation that unsafe scaffolds arise without explicitly prompting the Meta Agent to make them unsafe, modeling an actor unintentionally exposing vulnerabilities through scaffolding, although selection still optimizes harm. The reward-hacking explanation, performance-stagnation hypotheses, and stated limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix E reports approximate costs of $600 for blue, $115 for red, and $400 for capability-only experiments, including a blue-mode model-cost breakdown and the dated GPT-4o mini identifier. The reported code location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds PromptBreeder (Fernando et al., 2023), distinguishing prompt evolution from AgentBreeder's evolution of whole scaffolds. Existing comparisons with ADAS, EvoAgent, EvoMAC, ComfyAgent, Gödel Agent, and FunSearch remain; bibliographic reformatting does not otherwise change positioning.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and selected result passages, standardizes scaffold terminology, and updates the title and author information. Experiments are reordered from capability/blue/red to blue/red/capability ablation. Most main sections, methodological prose, discussion, and prompt instructions are retained.

P2.justification: The main document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column ICLR format. Algorithm 1 moves beside Figure 1, tables are relocated and reformatted, and descriptive result-row labels become mathematical expressions. New Figures 2–3 add evolutionary-population displays. These constitute substantial visual restructuring beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful plots and reproducibility details, but its stronger headline insufficiently qualifies the unchanged capability–safety tradeoff. In Table 1, the DROP scaffold achieving 86.0 safety has 62.0 F1, versus 71.4 F1 for the seed with 40.8 safety; the 79.0-F1 scaffold instead achieves 46.4 safety. Linking the 79.4% average safety uplift to maintained capability obscures this distinction. This weakening of the central claim's fidelity outweighs the limited documentation gains.
